CITY OF FOLKSTON Distilled Spirits Ordinance An ordinance to provide for the regulation, licensing, and taxing the sale of distilled spirits by the drink for consumption on the premises for the protection of public health, interest, and general welfare of the City of Folkston (the “City’”) and related provisions.

- (a) Definitions. Unless otherwise assigned herein, all terms used in this ordinance shall have the same definitions as assigned in Title 3 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated.

- (1) Restaurant: a place where meals are sold to the public for consumption on the premises. A restaurant shall be open for at least two meals per day, shall always be prepared to serve meals when it is open, shall have a full service kitchen, and shall derive at least 50 percent of its gross receipts from the sale of meals.

- (b) License required. No person, firm, or corporation shall offer for sale or sell any distilled spirits within the City Limits of Folkston, Georgia without first obtaining the appropriate license herein required.

- (c) Application. Each applicant shall apply to the Clerk for the City for a license by written application on forms available from the Clerk.

- (1) All applications must be filed at least thirty (30) days prior to the date when such application is to be considered by the City Council.

- (2) After investigation, all applications for such licenses shall be presented to the Council for approval. If approved, the licenses shall be issued by the Clerk upon payment of the required fee.

- (3) No licenses shall be granted to any person who is less than 21 years of age.

- (4) If the owner of the establishment making the application is an individual, the application shall be made by such individual. If the owner of the establishment making the application is an entity, the application shall be made by an individual with the authority to obligate the entity and enter into agreements on behalf of the entity.

- (5) No licenses shall be granted to any person who is serving as an elected official or City Clerk for the City, nor shall any license be granted to any business in which any such person holds an interest.

- (6) At the time the application is filed with the Clerk, the applicant shall have a complete set of his or her fingerprints made by the Police Department for the City for the purpose of conducting a criminal background check. Additionally, any individuals who will serve in a supervisory and/or managerial position with respect to the sale of distilled spirits shall submit to a criminal background check as set forth above.

- (7) No person or entity shall be granted a license to sell distilled spirits by the drink for consumption on the premises unless it shall appear to the satisfaction of the City Council that applicant is of good moral character and the business which he or she represents enjoys a good reputation. In no event shall any such license be granted to any person who has been convicted of or plead guilty or nolo contendere to any felony or misdemeanor involving alcohol or drugs within the five (5) year period immediately prior to the filing of the application.

- (d) Application fee. Each new application shall be accompanied by a non-refundable application fee in the amount of $100.00. Said fee shall be paid by cash, cashier’s check, or money order made payable to the City of Folkston.

- (e) Investigation. The City Clerk shall inspect the application to ensure its compliance with this ordinance. The City Clerk or the designee of the City Clerk shall further investigate the character and reputation of the applicant, the accuracy of the information provided by the applicant, and the suitability of the location of the location of the establishment for which the license is sought.

- (f) Consideration of application. All applications filed with the City Clerk shall be presented and considered by the City Council in the order of their filing, provided at least thirty (30) days have elapsed after the date of filing and all necessary investigation has been completed. In determining whether to grant a license pursuant to the ordinance, the City Council shall consider, along with any other relevant information:

- (1) The applicant’s reputation and character;

- (2) If the applicant has previously held a license to sell alcoholic beverages which was suspended, terminated, or revoked;

- (3) Whether the proposed location for the establishment is primarily a business or residential neighborhood;

- (4) Whether the issuance of such a license would tend to diminish the property values of other properties in the same area; and

- (5) Whether the sale of distilled spirits as authorized by the license would cause a violation of any federal, state, or local law, regulation, or ordinance.

- (g) Annual license fees. The annual license fee for a license permitting the sale of distilled spirits by the drink for consumption on the premises is $500.00. The fee is non-refundable.

- (h) License period and renewal. All licenses issued hereunder expire on December 31 of each year and may be renewed without the need for a new application at the option of the City Council.

- (i) Non-Transferable. Any license granted pursuant to this ordinance is not transferable to another establishment or location.

- (j) Display of license. The license issued hereunder shall at all times be posted in a conspicuous place within the building where distilled spirits may be served. If the license is not so posted, the establishment shall not be authorized to sell distilled spirits.

- (k) Locations. Distilled spirits sold by the drink for consumption on the premises are permitted only in restaurants which have applied for and received a license from the City as provided hereunder.

- (1) Suspension or revocation of license. A license issued pursuant to the ordinance may be suspended or revoked if it is discovered that the licensee made any false or misleading statements in the application, the licensee is convicted of or plead guilty or nolo contendere to any felony or misdemeanor involving alcohol or drugs, the licensee violates the provisions of federal, state, or local laws, regulations, or ordinances regarding the sale of distilled spirits or alcoholic beverage, or for any other reason which would cause an application by the licensee to be denied or rejected if the licensee were required to reapply for the license.

(m)Excise taxes. There is an excise tax imposed, in addition to any excise tax levied by any other jurisdiction, on the sale of any beverage containing distilled spirits in the amount of three percent of the charge to the public for the beverage. The tax required hereunder shall be paid to the City no later than the 10 day of each month based upon the sales of beverages containing distilled spirits during the previous calendar month. The payment of the tax shall be accompanied by a report showing the quantity of beverages containing distilled spirits sold, the price charged for said beverages, and the amount of excised tax collected and remitted to the City. Failure to

make a timely payment of the tax and report as required hereunder shall result in a penalty equal to fifty percent of the total amount of excise tax due, in addition to the amount due.

- (n) Penalties. Any person, firm, or corporation who violates any provision of this ordinance shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than sixty (60) days or by a fine of not more than five hundred dollars ($500.00) or both such fine and imprisonment, in the discretion of the appropriate court.

- (0) Section not exclusive. The infliction of a penalty under the provisions of this ordinance shall not prevent the revocation of any permit or license or the taking of other punitive or remedial action where called for or permitted under Georgia Law, the provisions of the Charter of the City of Folkston, or this Code.

- (p) Severability. Should any provision or section of the ordinance by held invalid, such holding shall not affect the validity of any other section or provision hereof which is not of itself invalid.

- (q) Effective Date. This ordinance shall become effective upon its adoption by the Mayor and Council of the City of Folkston.
